einzeiler: Discussing Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Capcom's incredible year, and industry news.
kurzfassung: The hosts and guest Lewis Gordon analyze Capcom's ongoing success, highlighted by the release of Onimusha: Way of the Sword. They also discuss recent industry controversies surrounding studio layoffs and console pricing, alongside reviews of recent games. Finally, they wrap up with recommendations and fan pitches for original Star Wars games.
stichpunkte: Discussion of Capcom's career-best year and the critical success of Onimusha: Way of the Sword
Analysis of industry struggles, including studio furloughs at Bit Reactor after the launch of Star Wars Zero Company
Evaluation of legal defenses from console manufacturers regarding digital ownership and tariff refunds
Reactions to Nvidia's DLSS 5 release and its divisive impact on character rendering and game performance
Review of the cooperative puzzle adventure game Orbitals on Switch 2
Debate over outlier review scores, specifically addressing the online discourse around high ratings
Brief impressions of Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy and other late-summer releases
Listener email segment featuring creative pitches for a Hitman-style Star Wars bounty hunter game

clips.hook: Studio layoffs despite a successful game launch
clips.text: The majority of a startup studio's workforce was furloughed without pay right before their game came out because funding ran dry, compounded by internal co-founder disputes.

clips.hook: Characters look cooked under AI model filters
clips.text: Graphic enhancements make character faces appear excessively over-detailed with harsh shadows and wrinkles, resembling someone who has spent too much time under a sunbed.

clips.hook: Only one digital copy available for the entire world
clips.text: A corporate legal argument implies that digital video games are finite physical items where the first person to make a purchase completely corners the market.

clips.hook: Capcom's era of stagnation versus its current golden age
clips.text: A prominent developer candidly attributes a company's modern turnaround to learning from past widespread failures and bringing game creation back home.

clips.hook: Would Ocarina of Time receive a low score today?
clips.text: A rhetorical question questions whether modern internet discourse and changing critical standards would ruin the reception of a classic masterpiece released today.

beschreibung:
Ben, Steve Ahlman, Matt James, and Lewis Gordon get together to ask: How does Capcom keep killing it? First, they run down some recent gaming news, including a lackluster Sony State of Play, a 'GTA'-driven bump in console sales, 'Star Wars Zero Company' maker Bit Reactor's furloughed workforce, the backlash to Nvidia's DLSS 5 AI upscaling tech, and two dubious arguments in legal filings by the major console manufacturers. After that, they share their reviews of 'Onimusha: Way of the Sword' and discuss Capcom's incredible run leading up to and throughout 2026, with insights from Lewis's reporting for The Ringer on the company's comeback. Finally, they provide their impressions of two other recent releases, 'Orbitals' and 'Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy.'

Read Lewis's piece here: https://www.theringer.com/2026/09/03/video-games/how-capcom-cracked-the-code-of-game-development-onimusha-resident-evil-pragmata
